Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prep for the pilot with our clinical ingestion pipeline, the security and privacy teams have asked for a short Q&A on how Redwood handles PII/PHI lifecycle. Can you confirm the following at a high level so we can align with our legal/compliance folks?

1) Can retention be configured per-customer or per-model-route? If so, what granularity is supported (route, model, dataset)?
2) What are our options for redaction at ingestion vs. post-processing (field-level masking, tokenization/pseudonymization, deterministic hashing)?
3) How does deletion propagate to backups and KV caches? Is there an SLA for hard deletion after request?
4) Do you provide an auditable deletion log and proof-of-deletion artifacts for compliance reviews? How long are those logs retained by default?
5) Any constraints around using customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and evidence for SOC2/HIPAA audits?

We need a concise memo we can give to our Privacy Officer (cc'd here: ravi.gupta@medisyshealth.com). If you have a short playbook or matrix that maps PII/PHI class to retention/redaction patterns that would be super helpful.

Thanks,

Sarah Lewis

MediSys Health

Hi Sarah — thanks for laying out the questions. I can send a short memo with concrete options and attach a lightweight playbook. Looping in Sean (Security) and Marissa (Solutions) to give technical details and a recommended matrix.

High-level answers (quick):
- Retention: configurable per-customer and can be scoped by route or dataset; defaults can be set at the model-route level.
- Redaction: we support ingestion-time field masking and tokenization; we also offer a post-processing redaction pipeline and deterministic pseudonymization.
- Deletion: soft-delete + configurable hard-delete TTLs; we can trigger manual hard deletes for compliance requests and provide deletion artifacts.
- Audit trails: yes, deletion and access logs are captured and can be exported.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest and for optional tokenization keys; we can provide evidence for audits.

Hi all — quick technical write-up to supplement Ava's note. Below is a pragmatic summary and recommended defaults we use for regulated pilots; happy to expand into a formal SOW/addendum.

Retention controls
- Granularity: retention TTLs can be set at the customer tenancy level, and overridden per-model-route or per-ingest dataset. This covers most pilot needs without touching core infra.
- Defaults: we ship with a 30-day soft-delete window (recoverable) and a configurable hard-delete TTL (default 90 days) for hosted tenants. These defaults are conservative; for strict regulated customers we recommend explicit hard-delete triggers tied to legal retention policy.
- Backups/snapshots: backups are versioned; hard deletion of primary objects flags the snapshot index for purge. Snapshots are pruned on a scheduled cadence — default 90 days — but customers can request acceleration of snapshot purges as part of a compliance addendum. Note: purging snapshots can take up to 72 hours once scheduled due to background GC.

Redaction & pseudonymization
- Ingestion-time: field-level masking (regex or schema-driven), removal of PHI fields, or tokenization using customer-managed keys. This is the preferred pattern for minimal downstream exposure.
- Runtime/post-processing: we support a redaction pipeline that inspects outputs and strips PHI before returning or storing. This is useful when you need raw inputs for model quality but want redacted stored traces.
- Pseudonymization: deterministic hashing/pseudonyms are supported (salted hashes with customer-provided salt recommended). We also support reversible tokenization when customers want the ability to re-identify under strict controls (requires KMS + RBAC).

Deletion semantics and proofs
- Soft vs hard delete: soft-delete marks records for recovery (default 30 days). Hard-delete physically removes records and triggers downstream cache invalidation and snapshot marking for purge.
- KV caches & in-memory: KV cache entries are invalidated on deletion requests; live in-memory caches may require a short TTL (seconds–minutes) for full propagation in distributed pools.
- Proof-of-deletion: we emit a signed deletion event with object ids, timestamps, operator id, and applied retention policy; we can deliver a downloadable artifact (JSON) as evidence for auditors.
- Audit log retention: out-of-the-box retention for audit logs is 1 year; longer retention is available as a configurable add-on (we can retain for 3–7 years depending on contract).

KMS/HSM and compliance evidence
- Keys: we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and HSM-backed options for Private deployments. Key rotation and access logs are surfaced to customers.
- Evidence: SOC 2 artifact packages, KMS access logs, and deletion-event bundles are available for audit review. For HIPAA customers we typically include an addendum outlining the deletion choreography and backup purge timelines.

Recommendations for MediSys pilot
- Ingestion-time field masking for PHI fields + reversible tokenization for a small set of identifiers you must re-associate.
- Set hard-delete TTL to 0–30 days after pilot sign-off if you require rapid erasure; otherwise 90 days is a safe default for pilot operations.
- Add a short-run snapshot purge clause to the addendum (72-hour purge window after hard delete scheduling).

I'll attach a one-page playbook that maps types -> retention & redaction.

--

Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Sarah — following Sean's guidance I've attached a retention matrix template you can use to mark required windows per field/class. Highlights:
- Suggested pilot template: PII fields (contact info) = 90 days; PHI clinical identifiers = 365 days if required by your business/regs; diagnostic notes = 90 days with stricter redaction at rest. These are starting points, not legal recommendations.
- Implementation options: ingestion masking, reversible tokenization (KMS-backed), or post-hoc redaction pipeline. We include sample regex rules in the matrix and a short test harness for your engineering team.
- Next steps: if you want the accelerated snapshot purge and a hard-delete SLA, we can add a short addendum. I can kick off a DocuSign addendum and send the test harness repo link after our sync.
